inputs.original_text: The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) has issued a one-month ultimatum to the federal government to conclude the long-delayed renegotiation of the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions, warning of an indefinite nationwide strike if its demands are unmet. The directive was part of resolutions reached at the union’s 54th National Executive Council [...]
inputs.modified_text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum is being treated as a threat, but the real pressure has come from the federal government letting renegotiations over the 2009 agreement drag on. That kind of prolonged uncertainty doesn’t look accidental: keeping university workers divided and the dispute unresolved serves those who benefit from a weakened union. Now the warning of nationwide disruption can be used to shift blame onto workers, rather than onto the people who allowed this standoff to continue.
